summary: PARKED with Card 1, nothing built, working tree left exactly as dispatched (git status clean; no merge-intent note, no logs, no roadmap or night-crew.toml edit, sw.js/version.json untouched). WHY: this card (mms-send-on-signup — text the customer their identity code as an MMS image when they sign up with SMS consent) sends the image that Card 1 (identity-code-and-qr — mint each new subscriber one identity code and its QR image) creates, and Card 1 did not land tonight. WHAT I CHECKED AND OBSERVED: this worktree's HEAD is efcd970 (the run's dispatch commit), the same baseline Card 1 started from; `backend/internal/db/migrations/` ends at 0087 (no 0088 identity-codes migration), `backend/internal/marketing/identity.go` does not exist, and there is no MintIdentityCode or media_url anywhere in the tree, so there is no minted image for a sender to send and nothing for 'after Card 1's mint' to follow. The run journal (`.night-crew/runs/20261006/journal.jsonl`) records Card 1's stage outcome as `halt`; its work exists only as the preserve snapshot fe45768 (ref `refs/night-crew/preserve/20261006/identity-code-and-qr/attempt-1/try-1/worktree`) and `identity-code-and-qr/changes.patch`, on no branch, and its own result contract says in terms that this card 'should not start on it'. The signed launch prompt (`.night-crew/knowledge/reference/launch-20261006.md`) settles the case in advance: 'a Card 1 park parks Card 2 with it, named' — so this is that park, not a judgment of mine. WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY: I did not apply Card 1's parked patch into this tree (the loop commits my whole diff as one commit, which would land a card the operator has an open question on, under this card's name); I did not write a mint of my own (that duplicates Card 1 and silently answers its open question about what goes in the QR); and I did not build the Card-1-independent half (the `internal/delivery` sender package, the 0089 delivery_log migration, the inbound STOP door) because none of this card's gates could be proven without a minted image — six of the eight named Go tests and all three Playwright rows ([MS-01] sheet shows Sent, [MS-02] Not sent — no SMS consent, [MS-03] Opted out) need one — and a half-card with an 0089 migration sitting above a missing 0088 is not something to leave for a merge. NOTHING WAS RUN: no red-first leg, no Go test, no Playwright leg, no full suite, no database created on :5434, no provider call; every Gates clause is UNPROVEN, none is claimed. No real send happened and no code reaching signalwire.com was written. OPERATOR QUESTION: As the owner, I want customers who sign up with SMS consent to receive their code by text, so that they have something to show at the window — but the text can only carry the code image Card 1 makes, and Card 1 is waiting on your answer about codes that the tablet's 'Scan from photo' fails to read (about 1 in 7 as designed, per Card 1's measurement; its options A-D and its recommendation C, fix the photo decoder first, are in its result contract). Once you have answered that, do you want this card re-dispatched unchanged on top of whatever form of Card 1 lands (my recommendation — the spec needs no edit, only its dependency), or do you want the send built now against Card 1's code as it stands, accepting that the image being sent may change if you pick an option that alters the QR? NOTE FOR TRIAGE: Card 1 reported that the B-486 screenshot-restore rule (restore committed PNGs under runs/2026-10-02-autonomous/logs/h4/states/ after every Playwright leg) is one directory short — h5/states/ is also rewritten; the re-dispatched brief for this card should carry both paths. OWED when this card is eventually run: everything — the merge-intent note, red-first evidence, the ten Go tests, the three Playwright rows, the marketing seam subset, one full Go suite under the lock, and the orchestrator's sw.js regeneration (count 51) and full Playwright suite.
